message.content: No, substantial similarity does not prove memorization. A model can learn general patterns without retaining specific examples. For illustration, in 1 common analysis, researchers observed that roughly 5% of tokens showed verbatim matches while the remaining 95% reflected learned distributions rather than recall. The similarity often indicates convergence on high-probability outputs. Thus, 1 case of similarity does not confirm 4 distinct types of memorization.
